title: airgapped-artifact-signing-and-offline-delivery-playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for upgrading Private (VPC / on-prem / appliance) deployments in air-gapped environments where the control plane and runtime artifacts must be packaged, signed, and transferred offline. Focus: artifact signing, offline delivery, terraform module changes required for customers that cannot reach Redwood-managed registries, and a small but robust validation & rollback decision tree.

Scope assumptions: 
- Target is appliance-style or VPC private deployments with zero outbound access to Redwood registries.
- Customers run our runtime as a set of containers or an appliance image; control plane components may be Kubernetes or a lightweight supervisor.
- We own the release artifacts (tarballs/container images/helm charts) and must provide verifiable signed bundles.

High-level flow (one-pager):
1) Build artifacts in CI/CD (release tag).
2) Create deterministic manifest (checksums + component versions).
3) Sign manifest with release-key (PKI), produce signature bundle.
4) Generate customer-specific delivery package (optionally encrypted).
5) Transfer via customer-approved channel (USB, SFTP, vendor courier).
6) Customer applies terraform changes referencing local artifacts.
7) Run preflight validations -> staged install -> smoke tests -> ramp -> post-validate.
8) If anomaly detected, run rollback sequence or contact SRE for assisted backout.

Preflight checklist (to run with customer 48–24 hours before delivery):
- Confirm inventory: node count, node labels, disk space >= package size + 20%.
- Verify KMS/HSM config for signature verification (public keys installed and trusted).
- Ensure terraform state snapshot and a copy of current infra manifests exist (store offline).
- Confirm CI artifact manifest checksum with customer (out-of-band).
- Agree on maintenance window and escalation contacts.
- Validate restore plan for persistent state (KV cache, model store backups).

Creating the signed bundle (release engineering steps):
- Produce deterministic tarball: tar --sort=name --mtime='2024-01-01' -cvf runtime-<TAG>.tar --transform 's,^,runtime-<TAG>/,' build_output/
- Compute checksums: sha256sum runtime-<TAG>.tar > runtime-<TAG>.sha256
- Generate manifest.json example: {
  "tag": "<TAG>",
  "components": [
    {"name":"runtime","file":"runtime-<TAG>.tar","sha256":"<hash>","type":"tar"},
    {"name":"controlplane","chart":"controlplane-<TAG>.tgz","sha256":"<hash>","type":"helm"}
  ]
}
- Sign manifest: cosign sign-blob --key release.key manifest.json > manifest.signature
- Package deliverable: tar -czf redwood-airgap-<TAG>-bundle.tgz manifest.json manifest.signature *.tar *.tgz
- Optionally encrypt with customer public key: gpg --encrypt --recipient customer@org redwood-airgap-<TAG>-bundle.tgz

Terraform notes for customers (common pitfalls):
- We ship module snippets that point to local file urls (file://) or OCI with local proxy. Example change for module source:
  module "runtime" {
    source = "./modules/runtime-local"
    image_archive = "/opt/redwood/artifacts/runtime-<TAG>.tar"
  }
- If customers use terraform remote state, snapshot before applying.
- Provider lockfile: pin provider versions to avoid auto-upgrades during apply.
- IAM / service account changes: avoid rotating critical service accounts during install.
- Recommended: run terraform plan -> save plan -> run terraform apply with --auto-approve only after signoff.

Staged install strategy (low-risk path we recommend):
- Stage 0: Install control-plane components in passive mode (leader elections disabled), verify pods start and remain CrashLoopFree for 10m.
- Stage 1: Install runtime on 10% of nodes (label nodes: upgrade=canary), route small traffic via route-mirroring.
- Stage 2: If canary passes (metrics thresholds below), expand to 30% for 1 hour.
- Stage 3: Full rollout in waves, monitoring each wave for 15–30 minutes.

Canary validation metrics and thresholds (example, customize per customer SLOs):
- Token latency p50 increase < 10% and p95 increase < 20% vs baseline.
- Error rate (5xx from runtime slice) less than 0.5% absolute increase.
- Request success ratio > 99.0% during canary window.
- Memory RSS and GPU memory stable (no > 15% increase).
- KV cache hit rate change < 5% negative delta.
- If any threshold breached, trigger immediate rollback of canary nodes.

Post-deploy validation suite (local test harness we provide):
- smoke-check.py: verifies API ping, auth, basic generation response length and format.
- perf-check.sh: synthetic traffic generator (100 rps for 5 minutes) to collect latency histograms.
- consistency-checker: runs a set of golden prompts and diffs critical output tokens against baseline tolerance table (acceptance: token-level BLEU-like metric > 0.92).
- telemetry sanity: ensure traces contain route tags, token counts, and cost metrics.

Rollback decision tree (simplified):
1) Canary fails: automatic rollback of canary nodes to previous image, notify oncall + customer infra lead.
2) Partial rollout failure (wave N): pause rollout, triage logs/metrics for 20m. If root cause unknown or >1 hour to fix, roll back to previous stable wave and open PD incident.
3) Full rollout failure: if cross-cluster issues appear (control plane degraded), immediate coordinated rollback of control plane + runtime and execute state reconciliation script (preserve DB snapshots).

Rollback commands (examples):
- runtime rollback: tar xzf runtime-previous.tgz -C /opt/redwood/artifacts && terraform apply -var="image_archive=/opt/redwood/artifacts/runtime-previous.tgz" -target=module.runtime
- helm rollback: helm rollback controlplane <REV> --namespace redwood-system

Troubleshooting quick hits:
- If signature verification fails: verify public key fingerprint and re-check manifest sha256. Command: cosign verify-blob --key release.pub manifest.json --signature manifest.signature
- If terraform apply hangs: check provider plugin logs (~/.terraform.d/plugin-cache) and ensure time skew < 2 minutes.
- If model load errors seen: validate model tarball unpack path and permissions; check kernel driver for GPU nodes.

Communication/Coordination checklist (during maintenance window):
- Primary: oncall-sre@redwood.ai, Eng-private point, Customer infra lead.
- Share progress messages at start, canary start, canary pass/fail, full rollout completion.
- Keep Slack channel open and escalate to SEs for customer-facing messaging.

Postmortem signals to capture if anything goes wrong:
- Timeline of applied terraform changes and manifests (timestamped).
- Copies of manifests and signatures used.
- Telemetry snapshots pre/during/post (token-latencies, error counts, CPU/GPU mem).
- Artifact delivery logs (who transferred what and when).

Open engineering follow-ups (TODOs):
- Add automated cosign verification into our terraform module so customers can run a local terraform plan that verifies signatures before apply. (RFC: PD-4201)
- Build small delivery portal that mints one-time download keys for encrypted bundles for courier handoffs.
- Add a lightweight offline monitoring agent that emits health summaries that can be transferred back to Redwood via USB and validated automatically.

Notes / rough ideas (brainstorm crumbs):
- Consider embedding a tiny signature verification web UI as part of appliance console (customer can upload bundle and it will show checksums + signature details).
- Explore shipping change-sets (delta patches) instead of full tarballs for customers with limited bandwidth.
- Provide a terraform example repo: modules/runtime-local/ with README and 'apply-offline.sh' helper.

Appendix: quick commands and sample outputs:
- Verify manifest signature: cosign verify-blob --key release.pub manifest.json --signature manifest.signature
  expected output: {"critical":{"identity":{"docker-reference":"manifest.json"},"type":"message"},"optional":{...}}
- Compute sha256: sha256sum runtime-<TAG>.tar
- Example terraform snippet for local provider: provider "local" {}
